adds.title: LGBTQ people in prison — Italy section (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Wikipedia 'LGBTQ people in prison' (Italy section, article revision 22 Sep 2026): in 2010 it was reported that Italy was to open its first dedicated transgender prison at Pozzale (Tuscany), a decision welcomed by gay-rights groups; as of 2013 the prison had not been created. This is the only documented Italian special-unit initiative for trans prisoners — announced, never opened — meaning trans detainees remain within the ordinary men's/women's prison circuit.

adds.title: Italy 'to open first prison for transgender inmates' | BBC News
adds.summary: BBC News (Jan 2010): Italy announced it would open one of the world's first prisons dedicated to transgender inmates at Pozzale, near Florence (Tuscany), converting an almost empty medium-security prison to house trans inmates mainly convicted of drug-related offences and prostitution; Italian gay-rights groups welcomed the move. The plan was never realized (per 2013 reporting), so no dedicated trans facility exists and trans prisoners continue to be placed in ordinary facilities.

records.note: No Southern Italy-specific documented trans-prisoner placement case/ruling surfaced within budget; prison administration and placement policy are national, so the findings above govern. Placement practice follows legal (ID-document) sex rather than gender identity, with no special trans unit ever opened (Pozzale plan of 2010 unrealized). Wikipedia full-text search 'transgender prisoners Italy' surfaced the LGBTQ-people-in-prison article as top hit, whose Italy section carries only the 2010 Pozzale plan; no Sud-specific trans-prisoner housing or segregation case documented in the fetched sources.

adds.title: La doppia sofferenza delle trans in carcere | la Repubblica Inchieste
adds.summary: la Repubblica inchiesta (28 Aug 2013), 'La doppia sofferenza delle trans in carcere': documents that trans women in Italian prisons live with the 'double suffering' of being held in men's sections because official documents (carta d'identità) still list them as male; female hormones cannot be prescribed to detainees whose ID says male, decisions bounce between prison directors and doctors with no national guideline, and some facilities allow hormone treatment only if the detainee pays for it. The case of 'Smeralda' illustrates that placement follows legal/registered sex rather than gender identity.

adds.summary: BBC News (Jan 2010): Italy announced it would open one of the world's first prisons dedicated to transgender inmates at Pozzale, near Florence (Tuscany), converting an almost empty medium-security prison to house trans inmates mainly convicted of drug-related offences and prostitution; Italian gay-rights groups welcomed the move. The plan was never realized (per 2013 reporting), so no dedicated trans facility exists and trans prisoners continue to be placed in ordinary facilities.

records.note: No Sicily- or Sardinia-specific documented trans-prisoner placement case surfaced within budget; the national regime applies to both island regions. Italian Wikipedia full-text search 'detenuti transgender carcere italia' surfaced politician Alessandro Zan's proposal to guarantee free hormone therapy access to trans detainees (treatment-conditions lead, not a placement finding, not fetched) and the film 'Mery per sempre' set in a Palermo juvenile prison (a dramatization, not a documented case/ruling); neither is usable as a placement add. Documented national practice: ID-sex placement, hormone access discretionary and often self-funded, no special unit (2010 Pozzale plan unrealized).
